title: 20.3 An RFID-Inspired One-Step Packaged Multimode Bio-Analyzer with Vacuum Microfluidics for Point-of-Care Diagnostics
problem: Point-of-care (POC) biomarker detection today relies on paper-based lateral-flow assays (LFAs)—offering speed but poor quantitative accuracy—or centralized lab instrumentation that is bulky/expensive. Integrating CMOS with microfluidics faces packaging complexity (wire/flip-chip bonding) and requires external pumps/tubing.
motivation: Clinical deployment of low-cost, pocketable diagnostic devices demands integration of micro-scale sample handling with compact CMOS sensing, avoiding external fluid delivery systems.
method: RFID-inspired one-step packaged integration merges millimeter-scale CMOS circuits with vacuum-based microfluidics (eliminating syringe pumps). Multimode detection combines electrochemical, optical, or impedance sensing per target biomarker. Vacuum microfluidics passively transports samples without external actuation.
key_novelty: RFID-inspired single-package integration of CMOS + vacuum microfluidics removes need for external pumps and complex bonding, achieving pocket-sized form factor.
contributions: One-step packaged multimode biomarker detection (protein/DNA/RNA/cells) without wire bonding complexity
Vacuum microfluidics replaces syringe pumps for sample transport and reduces system footprint
RFID-inspired power/data transmission paradigm for passive fluid handling
Maintains quantitative accuracy superior to paper-based LFAs

metrics.other: Pocketable form factor, multimode biomarker detection

limitations: Not discussed in abstract; packaging yield and reliability data absent.
